page.layout: One printed page, single text column with two marginal note blocks on the left. Running head and page number at the top. No catchword or signature. The strip at the far right is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.head: Caput V.

head.i: Quænam ex reip. forma optima, & ecclesiæ atq; reipublicæ convenientissima sit.

main_text.p: ANceps hæc est, & varia disputatio, in qua non temere aliquid definiri debet, aut potest, cum magna ejus ratio in circumstantiis posita sit: singulæ etiam formæ suis laborentnævis, & ad extrema vitia facile degenerent. Degenera-tio & vitia Monarchiæ[?].Monarchia levi motu in tyrannidem profilit, in qua unus homo, divinarum & humanarum legum repagulis sublatis & ruptis, pro sua libidine grassatur, res alienas, ut suas, ad se rapiens, liberisq; hominibus, tanquam mancipiis, abutens.

Ac durius sane æquo dici videtur, contraque jus, quod Christus in peculii sui & servorum corpora, atque animas plenum obtinet, quod corporum passim proprietates in imperiis nostris personant, quando de subditis sermo est. Contra proprieta-tes corpo-rum, quas vocant.Salomo contra commendatur, quòd exteras gentes fecerit tributarias, præter pecuniarium tribu-tum & [?] serviles etiam operas quasq; ab eis exigens; de filiis vero Israëlis non fecerit servum ullum, aut mancipium, ut videlicet contra divini fœderis privilegium, præ gentibus aliis singulare, ad sordidas, aut Sclavonicas, vel serviles illis abuteretur operas; cum interim tamen servi ejus ef-[?]sent, ingenua videlicet servitute, & liberalibus officiis,

page.notes: Right edge strip is the neighbouring page and was left out. Doubtful readings: the marginal "Monarchiæ" is partly worn and read as Monarchiæ; the mark before "serviles" in the line "tributum ... serviles" is unclear and read as &; "ef- sent" at the line end is unclear, possibly "es-sent". Show-through from the reverse is not transcribed. Lower part of the right edge is blurred. Printed page number is 176.
